waivers.reason: Transitive through Expo asset processing at build time, on images committed to this repository. The app decodes no untrusted image dimensions. Advisory: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops

Reached only at build time through the Expo CLI (expo -> @expo/cli -> node-forge, and again via @expo/code-signing-certificates), which uses it to sign expo-updates manifests. This app declares no updates or codeSigning block in app.config.ts and never imports expo-updates, so it neither produces nor verifies a signature, and the shipped bundle contains no RSA verifier. No patched release exists at any version -- npm's only offered fix is a semver-major expo bump, which would change the SDK. Advisory: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements

Install-time only, and not in the shipped bundle. undici 6.29.0 is marked dev in package-lock.json and its sole dependent in the tree is node-gyp, which fetches prebuilt binaries while native modules are compiled on a developer machine. The app itself has no network layer at all -- PRIVACY.md and __tests__/unit/offlineFirst.test.ts both assert that there is no HTTP client anywhere under src/, and nothing under src/ references undici. A patched release above 6.29.0 exists, so this is a lockfile bump rather than a blocked upgrade; it is deferred only because dependency resolution is unavailable in the environment this waiver was written in, and it should be taken as soon as a tree can be re-resolved. Advisory: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on excessive content-encodings

Two copies, neither reachable from the app. node_modules/zod 4.6.5 is marked dev and is pulled in by eslint-plugin-react-hooks, knip and zod-validation-error -- lint and dead-code tooling, which parse this repository's own source and configuration. node_modules/expo/node_modules/zod 3.25.76 comes from @expo/cli and runs only while a build is produced. Nothing under src/ imports zod, so the shipped bundle contains no Zod validator and no oversized collection reaches one. The dev copy would clear on a bump to 4.6.6, but the advisory stays reported until Expo's nested 3.x copy moves: npm's only offered fix is expo 54.0.38, a semver-major downgrade from the SDK 55 this project is on -- the same position as the node-forge waiver above. Advisory: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
